words.gloss: wholesome in dry cough, fatigue, excessive fire, wasting of flesh
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)
n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: और वह सूखी खाँसी, श्रम, अत्यग्नि और मांसक्षय में हितकर है। भैंस का मांस स्निग्ध, उष्ण, मधुर, वृष्य, गुरु और तर्पण है।
english: And that is wholesome in dry cough, fatigue (śrama), excessive digestive fire (atyagni) and wasting of flesh (māṃsakṣaya). Buffalo meat is unctuous, hot, sweet, aphrodisiac, heavy and replenishing (tarpaṇa).
notes: SENTENCE: tat continues the gavya (beef) named in the preceding unit; line 1 completes that sentence. atyagni = excessive (digestive) fire, kept as a term.
lines_deva: स्निग्धोष्णं मधुरं वृष्यं माहिषं गुरु तर्पणम्
lines_iast: snigdhoṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ vṛṣyaṃ māhiṣaṃ guru tarpaṇam

words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: यह दृढ़ता, बृहत्ता, उत्साह और निद्रा भी उत्पन्न करता है। गुरु, उष्ण, मधुर, बलकारक, बृंहण और पवन को दूर करने वाली —
english: It also produces firmness, bulk, energy and sleep. Heavy, hot, sweet, strengthening, nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) and removing Vāta (pavana) —
notes: Line 1 continues the buffalo meat (māhiṣa) of the preceding unit. SENTENCE: the masculine plurals of line 2 describe the matsyāḥ (fish) named in the next unit.

words.gloss: from feeding on water-moss and grass

hindi: मछलियाँ स्निग्ध, वृष्य और बहुदोष कही गई हैं। शैवाल और घास खाने के कारण और निद्रा का त्याग करने के कारण
english: Fish are declared unctuous, aphrodisiac and of much doṣa (bahudoṣa). Because of feeding on śaivāla and grass, and because of avoiding sleep,
notes: bahudoṣa may mean 'producing much doṣa' or 'having many defects'; the literal 'of much doṣa' is kept. SENTENCE: line 2 gives the reason for the qualities of the rohita named in the next unit. śaivāla = water-weed (plain meaning, notes only).

hindi: रोहित (मछली) अग्नि को दीप्त करने वाला, पाक में लघु, अत्यन्त बलवान्, वर्ण के लिए हितकर, वात को हरने वाला, वृष्य, नेत्रों के लिए हितकर और बल बढ़ाने वाला है।
english: the rohita (fish) stimulates digestion, is light in digestion (pāka) and of great strength; it is good for complexion, Vāta-removing, aphrodisiac, good for the eyes and increases strength.
notes: rohita kept as the fish's name, no identification. mahābala may also be read 'giving great strength'.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: कछुआ मेधा और स्मृति उत्पन्न करने वाला, पथ्य और शोष को नष्ट करने वाला कहा जाता है। खड्ग का मांस अभिष्यन्दी, बलकारक और मधुर माना गया है;
english: The tortoise (kūrma) is said to produce intelligence and memory, to be wholesome and to destroy śoṣa (wasting). Khaḍga meat is held to be channel-clogging (abhiṣyandin), strength-giving and sweet;
notes: kūrma given its plain meaning (tortoise); khaḍga kept as the Sanskrit name, no identification (as khaṅga in chunk 1). śoṣa kept as Sanskrit, no modern identification. The neuter qualities in the next unit continue khaḍgamāṃsa.

hindi: (वह) स्नेहन, बृंहण, वर्ण के लिए हितकर, श्रम को नष्ट करने वाला और अनिल को दूर करने वाला है। धार्तराष्ट्र, चकोर, दक्ष और मोर के भी
english: it is oleating (snehana), nourishing, good for complexion, destroys fatigue and removes Vāta (anila). Of the dhārtarāṣṭra, the cakora, the dakṣa and also of the peacock (śikhin),
notes: Line 1 continues khaḍgamāṃsa of the preceding unit (neuter). dhārtarāṣṭra, cakora and dakṣa are kept as bird names, no identification; śikhin given its plain meaning 'peacock' (literally 'crested'). SENTENCE: the genitives of line 2 go with aṇḍāni 'eggs' in the next unit.

words.gloss: in those whose semen is depleted

hindi: और चटक के जो अंडे हों, वे उन लोगों में जिनका रेतस् क्षीण हो गया है, खाँसी में, हृद्रोग में और क्षत में हितकर हैं,
english: and of the caṭaka, the eggs that there may be are wholesome in those whose semen is depleted, in coughs, heart diseases and injuries (kṣata);
notes: caṭaka kept as the Sanskrit name (glossary decision), no 'sparrow'. kṣata may be read as persons with injury (kṣata, m. loc. pl. 'the injured'); the neuter 'injuries' is kept. The second ca links hitāni with the qualities in the next unit.
lines_deva: चटकानां च यानि स्युरण्डानि च हितानि च
lines_iast: caṭakānāṃ ca yāni syuraṇḍāni ca hitāni ca

hindi: वे मधुर हैं, विदाह न करने वाले हैं और तुरन्त बल देने वाले हैं। शरीर के बृंहण में कोई अन्य खाद्य मांस से बढ़कर नहीं है।
english: they are sweet, do not cause burning (avidāhin) and give strength at once. In nourishing the body no other food excels meat.

words.gloss: the pot-herb of pāṭā, śuṣā and śaṭī
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: इस प्रकार मांसों का यह तीसरा वर्ग कहा गया। अब शाकवर्ग: पाटा, शुषा और शटी का शाक, वास्तुक, सुनिषण्णक —
english: Thus this third group, that of meats, has been declared. Now the group of pot-herbs (śākavarga): the pot-herb of pāṭā, śuṣā and śaṭī, vāstuka and suniṣaṇṇaka —
notes: 'atha śākavargaḥ---' is a prose heading typed at the head of verse line 2 (the dashes are left out of the split); the verse line after it has 16 syllables. Line 1 closes the meat group. Plant names kept as Sanskrit, no identifications. SENTENCE: the list continues into the next unit. pāṭā is kept as printed; pāṭhā is possible (same syllable weights), but nothing in the chunk shows it, so no text_flag.

hindi: (इन्हें) ग्राही और त्रिदोषनाशक जानना चाहिए, परन्तु वास्तुक मल को भेदने वाला है। काकमाची त्रिदोष को शान्त करने वाली, वृष्य और रसायनी है;
english: one should know (them) as binding and destroying the three doṣas; but vāstuka loosens the stool (bhinnavarcas). Kākamācī pacifies the three doṣas, is aphrodisiac and rejuvenative (rasāyanī);
notes: vāstuka is in the binding list of the preceding unit and is excepted here with tu. bhinnavarcas is a bahuvrīhi 'by which the stool is broken'. The feminine qualities of the next unit continue kākamācī.

words.gloss: of too hot or cold vīrya

hindi: उसका वीर्य न अधिक उष्ण है न अधिक शीत, और वह भेदिनी तथा कुष्ठ का नाश करने वाली है। राजक्षवक का शाक त्रिदोष को शान्त करने वाला और लघु है;
english: it is neither too hot nor too cold in vīrya (potency), and it is breaking (purgative) and destroys kuṣṭha. The rājakṣavaka pot-herb pacifies the three doṣas and is light;
notes: Line 1 continues kākamācī. The neuter qualities in the next unit continue rājakṣavakaśāka.

words.gloss: for those with grahaṇī and arśas disorders
words.gram: m. gen. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)
n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: वह ग्राही है और विशेष रूप से ग्रहणी और अर्श के रोगियों के लिए प्रशस्त है। कालशाक तो कटु, दीपन और गर तथा शोफ को जीतने वाला है।
english: it is binding and recommended especially for those suffering from grahaṇī and arśas. Kālaśāka, however, is pungent, stimulates digestion and overcomes gara and swelling (śopha).
notes: grahaṇī, arśas and gara kept Sanskrit, no modern identification. kālaśāka literally 'black pot-herb'.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: कालाय शाक लघु, उष्ण, वात बढ़ाने वाला और रूक्ष कहा जाता है। दीपनी, उष्णवीर्या और ग्राहिणी, कफ और मारुत में —
english: The kālāya pot-herb is said to be light, hot, Vāta-increasing (vātala) and dry. Stimulating digestion, hot in vīrya and binding, in Kapha and Vāta (kaphamāruta) —
notes: kālāya is printed with long ā, kalāya (short a) in 97. kālāya may be the vṛddhi derivative 'of kalāya' (kālāyaṃ śākam, like naimbaṃ śākaṃ in 97, kausumbha in 110, pauṣkara in 119), so the long ā need not be a slip; the chunk does not settle whether one plant is meant. Printed spellings kept, no flag. SENTENCE: the feminine qualities of line 2 belong to amlacāṅgerī in the next unit.

words.gram: f. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: अम्लचाङ्गेरी प्रशस्त मानी जाती है, और वह ग्रहणी और अर्श में हितकर है। मधुर, पाक में मधुर, भेदिनी, श्लेष्मा को बढ़ाने वाली,
english: the sour cāṅgerī (amlacāṅgerī) is praised, and it is wholesome in grahaṇī and arśas. Sweet, sweet in vipāka (pāka), breaking (purgative), increasing Kapha (śleṣman),
notes: SENTENCE: the feminine qualities of line 2 belong to upodikā in the next unit.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: वृष्य, स्निग्ध और शीत, और मद का भी नाश करने वाली उपोदिका है। रूक्ष, मद और विष का नाश करने वाला, और रक्तपित्त के रोगियों के लिए प्रशस्त,
english: aphrodisiac, unctuous and cold, and also destroying mada, is upodikā. Dry, destroying mada and poison, and recommended for those with raktapitta,
notes: mada kept Sanskrit. SENTENCE: the masculine qualities of line 2 belong to taṇḍulīyaka in the next unit.
lines_deva: वृष्या स्निग्धा च शीता च मदघ्नी चाप्युपोदिका
lines_iast: vṛṣyā snigdhā ca śītā ca madaghnī cāpyupodikā

hindi: मधुर, पाक में मधुर और शीतल तण्डुलीयक है। मण्डूकपर्णी, वेत्र का अग्रभाग, कुचेला, वनतिक्तक,
english: sweet, sweet in vipāka and cool is the taṇḍulīyaka. Maṇḍūkaparṇī, the tip of vetra (vetrāgra), kucelā, vanatiktaka,
notes: taṇḍulīyaka is a derived name (-īya-ka) and is not split. SENTENCE: line 2 opens a list of pot-herbs whose qualities are given in the first line of unit 98. Plant names kept as Sanskrit, no identifications. vetra = cane (plain common name, notes only).

hindi: कर्कोटक और अवल्गुजक, पटोल, शकुलादनी, वृष के फूल, शार्ङ्गेष्टा, कठिल्लक सहित केम्बूक,
english: karkoṭaka and avalgujaka, paṭola, śakulādanī, the flowers of vṛṣa, śārṅgeṣṭā, kembūka together with kaṭhillaka,
notes: List continued from the preceding unit; plant names kept as Sanskrit, no identifications. śārṅgeṣṭā left unsplit (members unclear).

hindi: नाडी, कलाय, गोजिह्वा, वार्ताक, तिलपर्णिका, और जो कौलक, कार्कश, निम्ब का और पार्पटक शाक है —
english: nāḍī, kalāya, gojihvā, vārtāka, tilaparṇikā, and the pot-herb that is kaulaka, kārkaśa, of nimba (naimba) and pārpaṭaka —
notes: nāḍī here is a plant name in a list of pot-herbs, not the disease nāḍī. kalāya (short a) is distinct in print from kālāya earlier in this chunk; neither is changed. naimba is a derived adjective 'of nimba', not a compound. The predicate follows in the first line of the next unit.
lines_deva: कौलकं कार्कशं नैम्बं शाकं पार्पटकं च यत्
lines_iast: kaulakaṃ kārkaśaṃ naimbaṃ śākaṃ pārpaṭakaṃ ca yat

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: (वह) कफ और पित्त को हरने वाला, तिक्त और शीत है, और पाक में कटु होता है। सभी सूप्य शाक, फञ्जी, चिल्ली, कुतुम्बक,
english: removes Kapha and Pitta, is bitter and cold, and becomes pungent in digestion (vipāka). All the pot-herbs fit for soup (sūpyaśāka), phañjī, cillī, kutumbaka,
notes: Line 1 is the predicate of the list that runs from unit 95 line 2 to unit 97. Line 2 opens a new list whose qualities are given in unit 103.

words.gram: n. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: और सब आलुक पत्तों सहित, कुटिञ्जर, शण और शाल्मलि के फूल, कर्बुदार, सुवर्चला,
english: and all the ālukas with their leaves, kuṭiñjara, the flowers of śaṇa and śālmali, karbudāra, suvarcalā,
notes: āluka kept as Sanskrit, no identification. śaṇa = hemp (plain common name, notes only).

hindi: निष्पाव, कोविदार और पत्तुर, चुच्चुपर्णिका, कुमारजीव, लोट्टाक, पालङ्क्या और उसी प्रकार मारिष,
english: niṣpāva, kovidāra and pattura, cuccuparṇikā, kumārajīva, loṭṭāka, pālaṅkyā and likewise māriṣa,
notes: List continued; plant names kept as Sanskrit, no identifications.

hindi: कलम्ब, नालिका और सूरी, कुसुम्भ और वृकधूमक, लक्ष्मणा और प्रपुन्नाड, नलिनीका, कुठेरक,
english: kalamba, nālikā and sūrī (or āsūrī), kusumbha and vṛkadhūmaka, lakṣmaṇā and prapunnāḍa, nalinīkā, kuṭheraka,
notes: kalambanālikāsūryaḥ is read as a dvandva ending in a feminine ī-stem, nom. pl. -yaḥ (as nadī -> nadyaḥ); the last member may be sūrī or āsūrī (nālikā + āsūryaḥ gives the same print), so it is uncertain; the plural agrees with a three-member dvandva and nothing is changed. vṛkadhūmaka (lit. wolf-smoke) is kept as one name.

hindi: लोणिका और यवशाक, कुष्माण्डक, अवल्गुज, यातुक, शालकल्याणी, त्रिपर्णी, पीलुपर्णिका —
english: loṇikā and the barley pot-herb (yavaśāka), kuṣmāṇḍaka, avalguja, yātuka, śālakalyāṇī, triparṇī, pīluparṇikā —
notes: kuṣmāṇḍaka is printed with short u; kūṣmāṇḍa with long ū appears later in this chunk; the metre is not affected, so nothing is changed. avalguja here and avalgujaka in unit 96 appear in two different lists; kept as printed. The predicate of this list follows in the next unit.

hindi: (यह) शाक गुरु और रूक्ष है, प्रायः विष्टम्भ करके पचता है, मधुर और शीतवीर्य है, और मल का भेदन करने वाला है।
english: (this) pot-herb is heavy and dry, is mostly digested after causing obstruction (viṣṭambha), is sweet and cold in vīrya, and breaks up the faeces.
notes: Predicate of the list running from unit 98 line 2 to unit 102.
lines_deva: शाकं गुरु च रूक्षं च प्रायो विष्टभ्य जीर्यति
मधुरं शीतवीर्यं च पुरीषस्य च भेदनम्
lines_iast: śākaṃ guru ca rūkṣaṃ ca prāyo viṣṭabhya jīryati
madhuraṃ śītavīryaṃ ca purīṣasya ca bhedanam

hindi: उबाला हुआ, रस निचोड़ा हुआ और स्नेह से भरपूर वह (शाक) प्रशस्त माना जाता है। शण, कोविदार, कर्बुदार और शाल्मलि का
english: It is praised boiled (svinna), with its juice squeezed out, and rich in fat (sneha). The flower of śaṇa, kovidāra, karbudāra and śālmali
notes: svinna literally 'sweated', i.e. cooked with moist heat (boiled or steamed). SENTENCE: the genitives of line 2 go with puṣpam in the next unit.

words.gloss: young leaves of nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa, padma etc.
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (bahuvrīhi with ādi)

hindi: फूल ग्राही है और विशेष रूप से रक्तपित्त में प्रशस्त है। न्यग्रोध, उदुम्बर, अश्वत्थ, प्लक्ष, पद्म आदि के पल्लव
english: is binding and recommended especially in raktapitta. The young leaves (pallava) of nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa, padma and the like
notes: Plain common names (standard): nyagrodha = banyan, udumbara = cluster fig, aśvattha = sacred fig (pipal), padma = lotus; plakṣa is left unidentified. The qualities of the pallavas follow in the next unit.
lines_deva: पुष्पं ग्राहि प्रशस्तं च रक्तपित्ते विशेषतः
lines_iast: puṣpaṃ grāhi praśastaṃ ca raktapitte viśeṣataḥ

hindi: कषाय, स्तम्भन, शीत और पित्तातिसार के रोगियों के लिए हितकर हैं। वत्सादनी वायु को नष्ट करती है, और कफ को गण्डीर और चित्रक,
english: are astringent, checking (stambhana), cold and wholesome for those with Pitta-type diarrhoea (pittātisāra). Vatsādanī destroys Vāta (vāyu), and Kapha, gaṇḍīra and citraka,
notes: hanyāt is an optative of general statement, rendered 'destroys'; the verb is understood again, in the dual, with gaṇḍīracitrakau. SENTENCE: the list of Kapha-destroyers continues in the next unit. vatsādanī (lit. calf-food) kept as one name.

hindi: श्रेयसी और बिल्वपर्णी; परन्तु बिल्व का पत्ता वात को दूर करता है। भण्डी, शतावरी का शाक, बला, और जो जीवन्तिक है,
english: śreyasī and bilvaparṇī; but the leaf of bilva dispels Vāta. Bhaṇḍī, the śatāvarī pot-herb, balā, and that which is jīvantika,
notes: Line 1 continues the Kapha-destroyers of the preceding unit. SENTENCE: line 2 opens a list whose predicate is in the first line of the next unit.
lines_deva: श्रेयसी बिल्वपर्णी च बिल्वपत्रं तु वातनुत्
भण्डी शतावरीशाकं बला जीवन्तिकं च यत्
lines_iast: śreyasī bilvaparṇī ca bilvapatraṃ tu vātanut
bhaṇḍī śatāvarīśākaṃ balā jīvantikaṃ ca yat

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: और पर्वणी और पर्वपुष्पी का (शाक) — (ये) वात और पित्त को हरने वाले माने गए हैं। लाङ्गलकी और उरुबूक का (शाक) लघु, मल को भेदने वाला और तिक्त है;
english: and (the pot-herb) of parvaṇī and of parvapuṣpī are held to remove Vāta and Pitta. (The pot-herb) of lāṅgalakī and urubūka is light, loosens the faeces (bhinnaśakṛt) and is bitter;
notes: The genitives parvaṇyāḥ, parvapuṣpyāḥ and lāṅgalakyurubūkayoḥ depend on an understood śākam. vātapittaharaṃ smṛtam (neuter singular, collective) is the predicate of the whole list from unit 107 line 2 (bhaṇḍī ... parvapuṣpī). Line 2 gives the qualities of the pot-herb of lāṅgalakī and urubūka; the next unit adds two more pot-herbs with ca ... ca, and whether these qualities extend to them is not stated.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

words.gloss: setting the downward passage in motion

hindi: और तिलवेतस का शाक और पञ्चाङ्गुल का शाक वात बढ़ाने वाले, कटु, तिक्त और अम्ल, और अधोमार्ग को प्रवृत्त करने वाले हैं।
english: and the tilavetasa pot-herb and the pot-herb of pañcāṅgula are Vāta-increasing, pungent, bitter and sour, and set the downward passage in motion.
notes: tilavetasa is kept as one name (lit. sesame-cane); pañcāṅgula (lit. five-fingered) kept as a name. Whether the qualities of the preceding unit's line 2 apply to these two as well is not stated; line 2 is read as the predicate of these two.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: कौसुम्भ (शाक) रूक्ष, अम्ल, उष्ण, कफ को नष्ट करने वाला और पित्त को बढ़ाने वाला है। त्रपुस और एर्वारुक मधुर, गुरु, विष्टम्भी और शीतल हैं,
english: The kausumbha (pot-herb of kusumbha) is dry, sour and hot, destroys Kapha and increases Pitta. Trapusa and ervāruka are sweet, heavy, obstructive (viṣṭambhin) and cool,
notes: trapusairvārukaṃ cannot be two separate words (trapusa has no ending), so it is a samāhāra dvandva. Plain common name (standard): trapusa = cucumber; ervāruka left unidentified.

words.gloss: relieving burning, thirst, exhaustion and distress
words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: और मुँह को प्रिय और रूक्ष हैं; परन्तु त्रपुस अत्यधिक मूत्रल है। और पूरा पका हुआ एर्वारुक दाह, तृष्णा, क्लम और पीड़ा को दूर करता है।
english: pleasing to the mouth and dry; but trapusa is exceedingly diuretic. And ervāruka, fully ripe, relieves burning, thirst, exhaustion (klama) and distress.
notes: ārti may be read with klama only ('the distress of exhaustion') or as a separate member; the separate member is kept.
lines_deva: मुखप्रियं च रूक्षं च मूत्रलं त्रपुसं त्वति
lines_iast: mukhapriyaṃ ca rūkṣaṃ ca mūtralaṃ trapusaṃ tvati

words.gram: n. nom. pl., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: अलाबू मल का भेदन करने वाले, रूक्ष, शीत और गुरु हैं। चिर्भट और एर्वारुक उसी प्रकार के हैं, परन्तु वे मल-भेद में हितकर हैं।
english: Alābus loosen the faeces and are dry, cold and heavy. Cirbhaṭa and ervāruka are likewise, but they are wholesome in loose stool (varcobheda).
notes: varcobhedahite is read as printed: varcobheda-hite 'wholesome in loose stool' (n. nom. du.), like grahaṇyarśohitā (93); tu contrasts it with the stool-loosening alābus of line 1, so tadvat is taken with their other qualities (dry, cold, heavy). 'Wholesome for loosening the stool' is the other sense of the same compound. A division varcobhede 'hite 'unwholesome in loose stool' would need the vowel e, which is not printed, so it is not adopted and not flagged. Plain common name (standard): alābu = bottle gourd.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: पका हुआ कूष्माण्ड क्षारयुक्त, मधुर और अम्ल, उसी प्रकार लघु, मूत्र और मल को निकालने वाला और सब दोषों को दूर करने वाला है।
english: Ripe kūṣmāṇḍa is alkaline (with kṣāra), sweet and sour, likewise light, releases urine and faeces, and removes all doṣas.
notes: sṛṣṭamūtrapurīṣa is a bahuvrīhi 'by which urine and faeces are released'. kūṣmāṇḍa kept as Sanskrit, no identification.

hindi: केलूट, कदम्ब, नदीमाषक और ऐन्दुक विशद, गुरु, शीत और भली-भाँति अभिष्यन्दी कहे जाते हैं।
english: Kelūṭa, kadamba, nadīmāṣaka and ainduka are said to be non-slimy (viśada), heavy, cold and thoroughly channel-clogging (samabhiṣyandin).
notes: The adjectives are neuter singular, said of the four together. ainduka (lit. 'of the moon') kept as a name.
lines_deva: विशदं गुरु शीतं च समभिष्यन्दि चोच्यते
lines_iast: viśadaṃ guru śītaṃ ca samabhiṣyandi cocyate

words.gloss: the pralamba (hanging part) of the tāla

hindi: उत्पल कषाय और रक्तपित्त को हरने वाले हैं। उसी प्रकार ताल का प्रलम्ब उरःक्षत की पीड़ा को दूर करने वाला होता है।
english: Utpalas are astringent and remove raktapitta. Likewise, the pralamba ('hanging part') of the tāla removes the pain of chest-injury (uraḥkṣata).
notes: pralamba literally 'hanging down'; what part of the tāla is meant is not stated. Plain common names (standard): utpala = water-lily, tāla = palm. tathā may also mean that the tālapralamba shares the utpalas' qualities; 'likewise' keeps both readings.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

words.gloss: tarūṭa, bisa, śālūka, krauñcādana and kaśeruka

hindi: खर्जूर और ताल का सस्य रक्तपित्त और क्षय को दूर करने वाले हैं। तरूट, बिस, शालूक, क्रौञ्चादन, कशेरुक,
english: Kharjūra and the produce (śasya) of the tāla remove raktapitta and kṣaya (wasting). Tarūṭa, bisa, śālūka, krauñcādana, kaśeruka,
notes: śasya is the spelling printed for sasya 'crop, produce'; printed spelling kept, no flag. Plain common name (standard): kharjūra = date. kṣaya kept as Sanskrit. Plain meanings (notes only): bisa = lotus-stalk, śālūka = lotus-root. SENTENCE: the samāhāra dvandva of line 2 continues into the next unit, whose first line gives the qualities.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: शृङ्गाटक और अङ्कलोड्य गुरु, विष्टम्भी और शीतल हैं। कुमुद और उत्पल की नालें, फूलों और फलों सहित,
english: śṛṅgāṭaka and aṅkaloḍya are heavy, obstructive and cool. The stalks of kumuda and utpala, with flowers and fruits, are held to be
notes: Line 1 gives the qualities of the whole list from the preceding unit's line 2. Plain common name (standard): śṛṅgāṭaka = water chestnut. SENTENCE: the predicate of line 2 is in the next unit.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva used as adj.
m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

hindi: शीत और मधुर-कषाय, परन्तु कफ और मारुत को कुपित करने वाली मानी गई हैं। कषाय, थोड़ा विष्टम्भी और रक्तपित्त को हरने वाला माना गया है
english: cold and sweet-astringent, but aggravating Kapha and Vāta (māruta). Astringent, slightly obstructive and removing raktapitta is held to be
notes: SENTENCE: the neuter qualities of line 2 belong to pauṣkara bīja in the next unit.

words.gram: n. nom. sg. (v/b spelling of bīja)

hindi: पौष्कर बीज, और वह रस और पाक में मधुर है। बलकारक, शीत, गुरु, स्निग्ध, तर्पण और बृंहण स्वभाव वाला —
english: the seed of the puṣkara (pauṣkara bīja); it is sweet in taste and vipāka. Strengthening, cold, heavy, unctuous, replenishing (tarpaṇa) and nourishing by nature —
notes: vīja is the v/b spelling of bīja; printed spelling kept, no flag. puṣkara is read as lotus from the lotus-plants around it (the line does not say). SENTENCE: the masculine qualities of line 2 cannot belong to the neuter bīja; they belong to muñcātaka named in the next unit.
